<SPAN 2>SERVICES, RESELLER AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>THIS AMENDED AND RESTATED SERVICES, RESELLER AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and entered into effective as of June 27, 2013 (the “Effective Date”) by and between The Advisory Board Company, a Delaware corporation (“ABCO”), and Evolent Health, Inc. (f/k/a VPHealth, Inc.), a Delaware corporation (“Evolent”), (each, a “Party”, and collectively, the “Parties”).</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>RECITALS</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>WHEREAS, ABCO and Evolent entered into a Services, Reseller and Non-Competition Agreement (the “Original Agreement”), effective as of August 31, 2011 (the “Original Effective Date”);</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS, since entering into the Original Agreement, Evolent and ABCO have continued to explore ways to improve the efficiency and implementation of their relationship; and</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>WHEREAS, as a result of the foregoing efforts, the Parties have agreed to amend and restate the Original Agreement as set forth in this Agreement.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the above recitals, the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereto agree as follows:</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>1. DEFINITIONS. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>For purposes of this Agreement:</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>1.1 “ABCO Restricted Products and Services” means </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>(a) care management services including, but not limited to, traditional disease management services, direct patient outreach and other service-based care management offerings (e.g., readmissions management teams, nurse call centers, on-site care management teams); </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>(b) care management workflow software designed for and used by provider-owned payor organizations or other entities intending to conduct active care management campaigns targeted at managing population health/longitudinal outcomes (i.e, solutions that are the same as or substantially similar to (i.e. functionality that is redundant in substantial and material respects with) HealthPlaNet); </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(c) services primarily intended to support cost reduction and benefit changes for health system employees; </SPAN 14><SPAN 15>(d) consulting services comparable and competitive with blueprint consulting services offered by Evolent as of the Effective Date (“Blueprint Services”), </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>(e) Exclusive TPA Services or </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>(f) Crimson Care Registry products. </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>For the avoidance of doubt, Restricted Products and Services does not include behavioral health-related services or software (e.g., Askesis Development Group software), services similar to those offered by UPMC WorkPartners (e.g., “Take-a-Healthy-Step” or similar health and wellness programs, occupational medicine, on-site clinic implementation and administration, employee assistance services, absence management or workers’ compensation services), or software or solutions similar to those offered by EBenefits Solutions, LLC.</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>1.2 “Active Sales Process”, with respect to any Person as of any date on which Evolent proposes to add such Person to the list of Evolent Top Prospects, means such Person </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>(a) is not an Evolent Client as of such date and </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>(b) either </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>(i) has purchased ABCO Restricted Products and Services from ABCO prior to such date or </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>(b) was engaged in active discussions with ABCO about acquiring ABCO Restricted Products and Services (including, but not limited to, a review of the applicable offering of ABCO Restricted Products and Services) as of such date.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>1.3 “Affiliate” means any Person which Controls, is Controlled by, or is in common Control with, another Person.</SPAN 24>
<SPAN 25>1.4 “Business Plan” has the meaning set forth in that certain Intellectual Property License and Data Access Agreement between the Parties.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>1.5 “Change of Control” with respect to any entity means a transaction or series of related transactions in which a Person, or a group of related Persons, acquires from stockholders of the subject entity, the entity’s shares representing more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting power of such entity.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>1.6 “Confidential Information” means any and all technical and non-technical information, whether conveyed verbally, in writing, electronically or by any other means, including, but not limited to, trade secrets, source code, technology, know-how and proprietary information, techniques, plans or any other information relating to any research project, analysis, work in process, future development, scientific, engineering, marketing or business plans or financial, contractual or personnel matters relating to either Party or its present or future products, services, sales, suppliers, identity of and information relating to customers and prospective customers, customer or prospect list, prospective employees, investors or affiliates or other proprietary information disclosed or otherwise supplied in confidence by either Party to the other, to the extent that such information is provided pursuant to this Agreement by one Party to the other Party and is marked “confidential” or “proprietary” or that should be reasonably understood by the Receiving Party (based on the nature of the information or the context in which the information is disclosed) should be considered confidential. </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>Confidential Information will not include information to the extent that: </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>(a) such information is or becomes publicly available other than through any act or omission of either Party in breach of this Agreement; </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>(b) such information was received by the Receiving Party, other than under an obligation of confidentiality, from a third party who had no obligation of confidentiality to the other Party; </SPAN 30><SPAN 31>(c) such information was in the possession of the Receiving Party at the time of the disclosure or was independently developed by the Receiving Party, as reflected by the Receiving Party’s internal, written and dated documentation; or </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>(d) an applicable regulation, court order or other legal process requires the disclosure of such information, provided that prior to such disclosure the Disclosing Party will give notice to the other Party so that the other Party may take reasonable steps to oppose or limit such disclosure, so that the Disclosing Party does not disclose any more information than necessary to comply with such legal process. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>The burden of proof that Confidential Information falls into any one of the above exemptions will be borne by the Party claiming such exemption with documentation or other credible evidence.</SPAN 33>

<SPAN 35>1.8 “Evolent Clients” means entities under a current contract with Evolent for an implementation and/or long-term services contract. </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>1.9 “Evolent Top Prospects” means, as of any date, up to twenty (20) potential Evolent customers in the Evolent sales pipeline identified by Evolent that are not Evolent Clients as of such date, and </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>(a) are engaged in active discussions with Evolent regarding purchasing Evolent products and services and/or </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>(b) are under a current contract with Evolent for Blueprint Services or other services that do not constitute implementation or long-term services; provided, however, that </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>(i) the list of such potential Evolent customers may be updated by Evolent on a quarterly basis, and ABCO shall have the opportunity upon receipt of each such quarterly update to notify Evolent if any of the Persons added to such list are in an Active Sales Process with ABCO and shall therefore be removed from such list, and </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>(ii) no Person shall remain on the list of Evolent Top Prospects for more than </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>(x) twelve (12) consecutive months, in the case of potential Evolent customers without a signed agreement with Evolent, or </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>(y) twenty-four </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>(24) consecutive months, in the case of potential Evolent Clients that signed an agreement for Blueprint Services with Evolent before or within twelve (12) months of being added to the list of Evolent Top Prospects.</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>1.10 “Exclusive TPA Services” means certain services as set forth on Schedule 1 of the UPMC Reseller Agreement (as in effect on the Effective Date), to the extent that UPMC Health Plan, Inc., a Pennsylvania nonprofit corporation (“UPMC”), has the exclusive right to provide such services to Evolent, for resale by Evolent to its customers.</SPAN 44>

<SPAN 48>1.14 “Loss” individually, and collectively, “Losses” means all claims, liabilities, obligations, losses, costs, expenses (including, without limitation, legal, accounting and similar expenses), litigation, proceedings, fines, taxes, levies, imposts, duties, deficiencies, assessments, charges, penalties, allegations, demands, damages (including, but not limited to, actual, punitive or consequential, foreseen or unforeseen, known or unknown, fixed or contingent, and matured or unmatured), civil and criminal violations of Law, settlements and judgments of any kind or nature whatsoever.</SPAN 48>

<SPAN 53>2. SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED BY ABCO.</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>2.1 General Services:</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>2.1.1 Minimum Purchase. </SPAN 55><SPAN 56>The Parties hereby acknowledge and agree that Evolent has purchased from ABCO a minimum of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($200,000) of services (as described in Section 2.2.1) (the “Original Minimum Purchase”) for delivery between the Original Effective Date and the first anniversary thereof.</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>2.1.2 Statements of Work. </SPAN 57><SPAN 58>The specific description, price, service levels (if applicable) and other project, service, and/or customer-specific terms for a particular service that may be provided by ABCO to Evolent (each, a “Service”, and collectively, the “Services”) shall be set forth in a Statement of Work that will be created on a project by project basis.</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>2.2 Right of First Offer and Process for Invoking:</SPAN 59>
<SPAN 60>2.2.1 Applicable Services. </SPAN 60><SPAN 61>Throughout the Term, ABCO shall have the right of first offer to provide the following services to Evolent and Evolent’s customers:</SPAN 61>
<SPAN 62>(a) Physician practice management consulting and other physician practice management services;</SPAN 62>
<SPAN 63>(b) Physician incentive design services;</SPAN 63>
<SPAN 64>(c) Medical home development consulting services; and</SPAN 64>
<SPAN 65>(d) Performance analytics shared with physicians with the intent to improve outcomes.</SPAN 65>
<SPAN 66>2.2.2 Process for Exercising Right of First Offer. </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>Evolent shall notify ABCO in writing in the event Evolent desires to receive any of the above services (“First Offer Services”). </SPAN 67><SPAN 68>ABCO shall have a period of thirty (30) days (“First Offer Services Evaluation Period”) within which to conduct its evaluation and diligence with respect to providing such First Offer Services. </SPAN 68><SPAN 69>Evolent shall cooperate with ABCO and provide reasonable assistance and information to ABCO to enable ABCO to conduct its evaluation. </SPAN 69><SPAN 70>Within five (5) business days after the expiration of such First Offer Services Evaluation Period, ABCO shall notify Evolent in writing whether or not it wishes to provide such services to Evolent. </SPAN 70><SPAN 71>If ABCO elects to provide such First Offer Services, Evolent agrees to engage in good faith negotiations with ABCO, on an exclusive basis for a period of sixty (60) days, regarding the specific terms covering such First Offer Services.</SPAN 71>
<SPAN 72>2.3 Failure to Execute a Service Agreement for the VBC Innovation Center: The Parties acknowledge and agree that it was their intent as of the Original Effective Date to enter into a service agreement under which Evolent would engage ABCO to provide certain consulting, development and support services in connection with the creation, launch, implementation and ongoing support of a Value-Based Care Innovation Center (the “VBC Innovation Center”), in consideration for which Evolent would pay ABCO a fixed fee of Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars ($800,000) per year (“Fixed Fee”) for each of the first two (2) years of the term of such VBC Innovation Center service agreement. </SPAN 72><SPAN 73>The Parties acknowledge and agree that, notwithstanding the fact that they negotiated with diligence and in good faith the specific terms and conditions of such service agreement, the Parties were unable to reach an agreement with respect to the VBC Innovation Center. </SPAN 73><SPAN 74>Accordingly, the Original Minimum Purchase is increased to One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,200,000) (the “Minimum Purchase”) as follows: </SPAN 74><SPAN 75>(a) between the Original Effective Date and the second anniversary thereof, Evolent shall have purchased from ABCO a minimum of Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($700,000) of services for delivery on or prior to such second anniversary of the Original Effective Date), and </SPAN 75><SPAN 76>(b) inclusive of the purchases described in clause </SPAN 76><SPAN 77>(a), between the Original Effective Date and the third anniversary thereof, Evolent shall have purchased from ABCO a minimum of One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,200,000) of services for delivery on or prior to such third anniversary of the Original Effective Date); provided that, for purposes of this sentence, “services” shall include consulting, software, professional or analytic services provided from time to time by ABCO to Evolent (other than services in connection with the provision of any office space by or on behalf of ABCO to Evolent) or, pursuant to a joint written proposal by ABCO and Evolent, to any Evolent Client.</SPAN 77>
<SPAN 78>2.4 Reservation of Rights: </SPAN 78><SPAN 79>For the avoidance of doubt, Evolent is not precluded from offering and providing services directly to its customers, subject </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>(a) to (i.e., after ABCO has had the full opportunity to exercise) ABCO’s right of first offer to provide any First Offer Services in accordance with Section </SPAN 80><SPAN 81>2.2) and </SPAN 81><SPAN 82>(b) to Evolent’s compliance with its non-competition obligations as set forth in Section 6.2.</SPAN 82>
<SPAN 83>2.5 Designation of Relationship Managers: </SPAN 83><SPAN 84>In order to support the launch and ongoing success of the exclusive reseller relationship between ABCO and Evolent, each Party agrees to designate a senior level individual who will serve as the primary liaison and “go to” contact and relationship manager for such Party (each, a “Relationship Manager”). </SPAN 84><SPAN 85>Each Party’s Relationship Manager’s role and responsibilities would include: </SPAN 85><SPAN 86>(a) facilitating day-to-day communications between the Parties regarding customer-facing activities, such as marketing, promotional and sales activities and preparing and submitting bids, proposals, responses to requests for proposals, fee estimates, Statements of Work and project plans; </SPAN 86><SPAN 87>(b) receiving and submitting requests between the Parties for information and/or assistance; </SPAN 87><SPAN 88>(c) overseeing the efficient knowledge transfer and flow of information between the Parties; </SPAN 88><SPAN 89>(d) facilitating communications between the appropriate individuals within Evolent and ABCO, with respect to product and service offering development; and </SPAN 89><SPAN 90>(e) providing the first level of performance review or escalation in the event of a Dispute as provided in Section 13. </SPAN 90><SPAN 91>The Relationship Managers will meet regularly, but no less frequently than monthly, as reasonably necessary, to maintain a good working relationship between the Parties. </SPAN 91><SPAN 92>Each Party may change its Relationship Manager by giving the other Party reasonable notice as long as the change is implemented in a manner that does not cause any significant disruption to each Party’s business operations and business relationship.</SPAN 92>
<SPAN 93>3. FEES; PAYMENT TERMS; SHORTFALL.</SPAN 93>
<SPAN 94>3.1 Fees; Timing of Payments: Evolent shall pay ABCO the applicable fees for the Services performed by ABCO pursuant to a Statement of Work, as follows: </SPAN 94><SPAN 95>(a) unless the Parties otherwise agree in writing, a deposit of 50% of the total fees for the particular project shall be paid upon signing of the Statement of Work; </SPAN 95><SPAN 96>(b) ABCO will submit an invoice to Evolent for the balance upon completion of the work; and </SPAN 96><SPAN 97>(c) Evolent shall pay ABCO for such invoiced amount within thirty (30) days after receipt of such invoice.</SPAN 97>
<SPAN 98>3.2 Minimum Purchase and Shortfall: Evolent agrees to pay ABCO the Minimum Purchase. </SPAN 98><SPAN 99>If the aggregate amount of Services actually procured by Evolent from ABCO is not equal to or greater than </SPAN 99><SPAN 100>(a) Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($700,000) of services for delivery on or prior to the second anniversary of the Original Effective Date or </SPAN 100><SPAN 101>(b) inclusive of the purchase described in clause </SPAN 101><SPAN 102>(a), the Minimum Purchase of services for delivery on or prior to the third anniversary of the Original Effective Date, Evolent shall pay ABCO the amount of the shortfall (i.e., the difference between Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($700,000) or the Minimum Purchase amount, as applicable, less the sum of: </SPAN 102><SPAN 103>(a) the aggregate fees for the actual amount of Services procured; and </SPAN 103><SPAN 104>(b) any Credits (as provided in the next sentence) (the “Shortfall”), if any, on or before August 31, 2013 or August 31, 2014, as applicable. </SPAN 104><SPAN 105>In the event that ABCO refuses or fails, without reasonable cause, to provide any of the Services requested by Evolent (provided the scope of the Services requested is within the scope customarily provided by ABCO), the fees that would otherwise have been applicable had ABCO agreed to provide such Services would count as a “Credit”. </SPAN 105><SPAN 106>As of the date hereof, no such Credits have accrued.</SPAN 106>
<SPAN 107>4. TERM AND RENEWAL. </SPAN 107><SPAN 108>The initial term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and unless sooner terminated in accordance with the terms hereof, shall continue until August 31, 2016 (“Initial Term”). </SPAN 108><SPAN 109>Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically be renewed for another five-year term (“Renewal Term”) unless either Party elects to terminate this Agreement by providing the other Party with written notice of termination one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the current term. </SPAN 109><SPAN 110>(“Initial Term” and “Renewal Term” collectively, the “Term”).</SPAN 110>
<SPAN 111>5. REFERRAL FEES, SOLICITATION AND COMPETITION AND POST-CLOSING SERVICES.</SPAN 111>
<SPAN 112>5.1 Referral Fees:</SPAN 112>
<SPAN 113>5.1.1 During the Term, ABCO will pay Evolent a sales referral fee for any sale made by ABCO that resulted from a “net” new sale from a new customer that was not already in ABCO’s sales pipeline (i.e., a “warm lead”) or a then-current customer of ABCO generated directly by Evolent’s efforts and without any assistance from any ABCO employee or representative (including any Evolent employee that serves on the Board of Directors of ABCO), equal to 5% of the total ABCO revenue from the new customer during the initial twelve (12) months of services under the services agreement with such new customer.</SPAN 113>
<SPAN 114>5.1.2 </SPAN 114><SPAN 115>During the Term, Evolent will pay ABCO a sales referral fee for any sale made by Evolent that resulted from a “net” new sale from a new customer that was not already in Evolent’s sales pipeline (i.e., a “warm lead”) or a then-current customer of Evolent generated directly by ABCO’s efforts and without any assistance from any Evolent employee or representative (including any ABCO employee that serves on the Board of Directors of Evolent), in accordance with the following terms:</SPAN 115>
<SPAN 116>(a) ABCO will receive a one-time referral fee for any “employee health” diagnostic, consulting or broker services provided by Evolent to a Covered Health System, equal to the lesser of $20,000 or 5% of the total Evolent revenue from the Covered Health System during the initial twelve (12) months of services under the service agreement with such Covered Health System.</SPAN 116>
<SPAN 117>(b) ABCO will receive $50,000 per year for three (3) years for each health system joining Evolent as an Employee Health Platform Customer. </SPAN 117><SPAN 118>An “Employee Health Platform Customer” is defined as a health system purchasing diagnostic/consulting services and ongoing medical management/health plan services (i.e., care management, HealthPlaNet care management application, and the TPA platform, etc.).</SPAN 118>
<SPAN 119>(c) ABCO will receive $100,000 per year for three (3) years for a health system joining Evolent as a Platform Health Plan Customer. </SPAN 119><SPAN 120>A “Platform Health Plan Customer” is defined as a health system purchasing ongoing medical management services, ongoing health plan outsourcing services (i.e., TPA) and health plan management services for purposes of a licensed insurance entity with at least fifty thousand (50,000) lives (beyond the employee population).</SPAN 120>
<SPAN 121>(d) With the exception of making the introduction (either through an email or an in-person meeting) (to generate the “warm lead”), ABCO would not be expected to perform any actual duties or incur actual cost to receive a referral fee.</SPAN 121>
<SPAN 122>(e) The annual referral fees for each referral would be capped at the lesser of </SPAN 122><SPAN 123>(x) 5% of annual revenue generated by Evolent for the respective customer and </SPAN 123><SPAN 124>(y) the $50,000 or $100,000 figures described above, as applicable.</SPAN 124>
<SPAN 125>6. SOLICITATION AND COMPETITION.</SPAN 125>
<SPAN 126>6.1 Scope:</SPAN 126>
<SPAN 127>6.1.1 </SPAN 127><SPAN 128>Throughout the Term, ABCO agrees not to offer any ABCO Restricted Products and Services to </SPAN 128><SPAN 129>(a) any Evolent Clients or </SPAN 129><SPAN 130>(b) any Evolent Top Prospects; provided, however, that ABCO shall not be restricted from making any such offer to any Evolent Top Prospect or Evolent Client with whom ABCO was, at the time such Person was identified as an Evolent Top Prospect or became an Evolent Client, engaged in an Active Sales Process. </SPAN 130><SPAN 131>The foregoing restrictions shall not apply in the event of a Change of Control of Evolent or in the event that ABCO ceases to be a shareholder of Evolent.</SPAN 131>
<SPAN 132>6.1.2 </SPAN 132><SPAN 133>None of the foregoing would prohibit ABCO from:</SPAN 133>
<SPAN 134>(a) Marketing, offering, licensing or selling versions of any of its Crimson Population Risk Management products, or the successors to any such products, provided that such products, or the successors to any such products, are not the same as or substantially similar to (i.e., includes functionality that is redundant in substantial and material respects with) HealthPlaNet as it exists as of the Effective Date.</SPAN 134>
<SPAN 135>(b) Supporting employers with care management related best practices and research.</SPAN 135>
<SPAN 136>(c) Offering traditional “dedicated advisor” support in conjunction with ABCO’s traditional business intelligence offerings.</SPAN 136>
<SPAN 137>(d) Marketing, offering, licensing or selling its employer health product.</SPAN 137>
<SPAN 138>(e) Providing physician management consulting and other physician management services.</SPAN 138>
<SPAN 139>6.2 Restrictions Relating to Certain ABCO </SPAN 139><SPAN 140>Products and Services: Evolent shall not, until the earlier of </SPAN 140><SPAN 141>(x) ABCO’s ceasing to be a shareholder of Evolent or </SPAN 141><SPAN 142>(y) the seventh (7 ) anniversary of the date of this Agreement, promote, market, provide, offer or sellth </SPAN 142><SPAN 143>(a) unbundled software applications, consulting services that are offered by ABCO as of the date first written above. </SPAN 146><SPAN 147>For the avoidance of doubt, “unbundled” means on a stand-alone basis, instead of “bundled”, which incidental to the provision of such other Evolent products or services. </SPAN 149><SPAN 150>Notwithstanding any other provision hereof, the foregoing restrictions in this Section 6.2 shall survive a assets acquired.</SPAN 150>
<SPAN 151>6.3 Non-Solicitation or Hiring: During the Term and for a period of eighteen (18) months thereafter, Evolent shall not solicit or hire any of ABCO’s employees without ABCO’s prior written consent.</SPAN 151>
<SPAN 152>7. EXCLUSIVE RESELLER RIGHTS FOR FUTURE PRODUCTS.</SPAN 152>
<SPAN 153>In the event that Evolent creates a discrete or segregable product or service that can be sold to healthcare providers, Evolent shall notify ABCO in writing of such new offerings (“New Products”). </SPAN 153><SPAN 154>ABCO shall have a period of ninety (90) days (“New Products Evaluation Period”) within which to conduct its evaluation and diligence with respect to providing such New Products. </SPAN 154><SPAN 155>Evolent shall cooperate with ABCO and provide reasonable assistance and information to ABCO to enable ABCO to conduct its evaluation. </SPAN 155><SPAN 156>Within five (5) business days after the expiration of such New Products Evaluation Period, ABCO shall notify Evolent in writing whether or not it wishes to have the right to resell such New Products. </SPAN 156><SPAN 157>If ABCO elects to resell such New Products, Evolent and ABCO agree to negotiate in good faith on an exclusive basis for one hundred twenty (120) days the terms of a reseller agreement, under which ABCO would be the exclusive distributor (in addition to Evolent) of such New Products.</SPAN 157>
<SPAN 158>8. CONFIDENTIALITY.</SPAN 158>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination, expiration, conclusion of an evaluation, a determination that development cannot proceed, or cessation of interest qualifies when that event itself activates the duty. A request-only duty does not qualify. Nor does a party's unilateral decision not to proceed unless the clause treats that decision as the operative conclusion of the protected process.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete return-or-destruction duty together with its end-event trigger. Do not omit a governing introduction, and do not substitute a request trigger or a retention clause for the required end-event link.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational route for making copies, such as copies necessary for an authorized purpose or acknowledged backup creation. Prepared analyses or compilations do not by themselves authorize copying. A ban qualified by prior consent, and a remedy for unauthorized copying, are not affirmative permissions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language that affirmatively authorizes, requires, or acknowledges copy creation and its condition; access, disclosure, derivative-document coverage, consent qualifiers, and breach-remedy clauses are insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or later made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Require lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party or its representatives, with the source free of confidentiality restrictions, or a later non-confidential release that makes the information externally available. Independent development is different. Information supplied by a third-party vendor through the disclosing party is still disclosed through the protected channel and is not an acquisition permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release item and its governing exclusion introduction, including the condition on the source's authority or confidentiality duty.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure or access to employees, internal staff, or a defined representative class.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an operative permission and that employees or internal staff belong to the permitted class. A definition naming employees is insufficient without a disclosure route; a permission to consultants, agents, or affiliates alone does not establish employee sharing.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the disclosure or access permission and, if the permission uses a defined class, the definition proving employees are included, plus material need-to-know or confidentiality conditions.

guidance.when: A clause permits or addresses disclosure compelled by law, regulation, court order, governmental demand, or legal process.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether that compelled-disclosure event requires notice, consultation, or equivalent advance communication to the disclosing party, subject to any legal-permission qualifier. A compelled-disclosure exception without a communication duty is insufficient, as is notice of an unauthorized disclosure after it occurs.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the compelled-disclosure trigger and the notice or consultation duty, including cross-referenced or list-introduction text needed to connect them.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits use of confidential information or defined residual information beyond a transaction-specific or otherwise stated agreement purpose.
guidance.inspection: A permission to use protected information for any purpose, or for the recipient's general internal business purposes without tying use to the agreement's stated purpose, negates an exclusive-purpose restriction. Merely allowing copying, disclosure, or conduct of a proposed relationship does not establish this contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the affirmative broad-use permission and any definition needed to show that it applies to confidential information or information retained from it.

guidance.when: The agreement states who may receive confidential information and the exception is limited to employees.
guidance.inspection: If disclosure is prohibited to everyone except qualifying employees, and the complete agreement supplies no permission for consultants, agents, advisers, or other non-employees, the agreement negates permission to share with third parties. A consent-based possibility alone is not an existing sharing permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the employee-only exception and the governing prohibition, and verify that no independent non-employee disclosure route qualifies it.
